                                                                                                                                                            VETERANS UP FRONT
                                                                                                                                                            • Led by starting center Chandler Strong, the UNT offensive line contains five players who have each played
                                                                                                                                                            at least 20 games throughout their career.
                                                                                                                                                            • A former Freshman All-American, Strong transferred to UNT after spending the 2022-25 seasons at Geor-
                                                                                                                                                            gia Southern. He is the most experienced player on the offensive side of the ball with 39 career starts.
                                                                                                                                                            • Alongside Strong is returning senior Keon Johnson (32 GP), Texas transfer Neto Umeozulu (33 GP) and
                                                                                                                                                            Missouri transfer Johnny Williams IV (28 GP), who have all started every game this season.
                                                                                                                                                            • Senior letterwinner Dylan Shaw and juniors Willie Goodacre and Roberto Rodriguez have split time at
                                                                                                                                                            left guard, each starting at least one game this season.
                                                                                                                                                            • The veteran offensive line has been a key piece of the offense’s success, allowing just six sacks through
                                                                                                                                                            the first seven games of the season. That is 0.86 sacks allowed per game, which ranks top 10 in the FBS.

                                                                                                                                                            GET AHEAD,  STAY AHEAD
                                                                                                                                                             • Throughout his 10+ seasons as head coach, a clear formula for success for Neal Brown has been taking
                                                                                                                                                             an early lead and playing from out front. Brown’s teams are 62-6 when leading at the half and 64-4 when
                                                                                                                                                             leading after three quarters. UNT is 4-0 and 5-0 in those scenarios this season, respectively.
                                                                                                                                                             • Brown also owns a 54-16 career record when his team scores first.

                                                                                                                                                                     UNT at NAVY
                                                                                   Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium  •  Annapolis, Md.
                                                                                                                                  Oct. 24, 2026  •  Attendance: 33,166

POSTGAME NOTES
•                    The Mean Green win gives them a 2-2 split in all-time the series and snapped Navy’s
           eight-game home winning streak. UNT has now won the last two meetings – last
           season and Saturday night.
•                       The Mean Green eclipsed 40 points for the fourth straight game and the fifth time in
           their last six games.
•                       For the third time this season, UNT scored on each of its first three possessions, but it
           was the first time it has touchdowns on each of the first three drives. Against Charlotte,
           UNT had a field goal and two touchdowns. In the win over UNLV, UNT had two straight
           field goals and then a touchdown in its first three drives.
•                    UNT’s 49 points was the most allowed by Navy this season, eclipsing the 38 points
           allowed to UTSA last week.
•                    UNT had an offensive touchdown, defensive touchdown and special teams touchdown
           in the game – marking the first time since Sept. 15, 2018, at Arkansas that UNT scored
           a touchdown in all three phases of the game.
•                       Fifth-year QB Tayven Jackson finished 17 for 23 for 305 yards passing and three
           touchdowns. Jackson’s 305 yards gave him his fourth 300-yard passing game of the
           season and his career, and his fourth in just his past five games.
•                    Senior RB Jaheim White’s 174 rushing yards marked his 12th career 100-yard rushing
           day and his fifth for UNT. White is the only player in The American with six games this
           season of at least 100 total yards from scrimmage.
